findings.summary: Criterion 4 says only three files change, but the plan also changes docs/decisions.md and quietly rewrites the criterion as four files.
findings.evidence: Criterion 4 says: 'Only docs/spec.toml, crates/athena-core/src/design_surface.rs and CHANGELOG.md change'. The expected deliverables also list docs/decisions.md (modify). The plan's demonstration for criterion 4 observes four modified files without pointing out the conflict, so a verifier reading the criterion literally could fail it. Fix: Say in the plan, for example as a Decision or in the criterion 4 demonstration, that the expected deliverables add docs/decisions.md to criterion 4's list. Point out the conflict so the verifier judges against the deliverables list, not the three-file wording.
findings.location: Demonstrations, Criterion 4; reading criterion 4 vs Expected deliverables

findings.summary: In this repository, the main way the path rule misses a change is parallel unrelated decision entries. The plan's wording of the limit undersells that.
findings.evidence: plan.rs:537 and drain.rs:976 list docs/decisions.md in SHARED_APPEND_ONLY. Many jobs append to it, so a change that alters the surface and also adds an unrelated D-entry passes the check. The plan describes the gap as 'text appended with no new `## D<n>` heading'. But even the heading-based follow-up would not catch an unrelated new heading. Fix: In the doc comment and D172, also state that any new entry satisfies the rule, whether or not it concerns the changed surface item. Note that the heading follow-up narrows this gap but does not close it.

findings.summary: Each finding line repeats the zero counts for every kind with changes. Naming the changed items would be more useful.
findings.evidence: The example line is 'commands: 1 added, 0 removed, 0 changed, with no entry in docs/decisions.md'. `KindDiff` already holds the added, removed and changed names (design_surface.rs:600-604). Fix: Optionally list the item names, for example 'commands: added ask-x', so that a later wiring job can say what needs a decision.

summary: I read the code to check the plan's claims, and they hold. `diff` is at design_surface.rs:722. `SurfaceDiff::kinds()` is at :635 and `KindDiff::total()` is at :608. The tests module is at :773. `SurfaceInventory` derives Default and has public BTreeMap fields (athena-data records/design_surface.rs:12-27). OLY-A-12 sits at spec.toml:1760-1766 with mechanism `none`. D171 is the last entry in the decision log. `measure_problem` accepts labels that start with `not shown` (hestia.rs:1229). The xtask test only checks that the fields are filled in (spec.rs:194-213). The private `DECISION_LOG` constant is at run/checks.rs:7. No reader outside spec.toml names OLY-A-12. The criterion 2 test calls the real function on output from the real `diff`. It fails if the function always returns nothing, if it ignores the log, or if it always flags a change. The criterion 1 demonstration now honestly says the spec tests are only a well-formedness check. The dependents list covers the readers of spec.toml, decisions.md and CHANGELOG.md that I spot-checked. On soundness, the rule "the decisions file is among the changed paths" is coarse. Because decisions.md is a shared append-only file, an unrelated entry from the same change would silence the check. But the accepted reading and criterion 2 ask for exactly this rule. The plan states the limit, records the stricter heading-based follow-up, and does not wire the check into anything, so it refuses nothing. That is acceptable for this scope. Two minor points remain: criterion 4 lists three changed files but the plan changes four, and the word "decision" in the new text may need care.
